reference: GNU Coreutils du invoked by the system Bash in the harness. Parity scripts use GNU-supported options and small relative fixtures. Byte and human-size cases use apparent sizes so expected amounts do not depend on filesystem allocation.
coverage: Bash builtin type and short help metadata contracts
GNU apparent byte sizes for named operands and the default current-directory operand
Recursive directory totals, -a output, and maximum output depth
NUL-terminated output and paths containing spaces
Block-size ceiling, grand totals, binary human-readable units, and decimal SI units
Default symlink handling, command-line dereferencing, and recursive dereferencing
Guest compatibility pass 6 (G90): GNU diagnostic wording for operand and usage errors.

Guest pass 10 (G144) against GNU coreutils 9.7: -h/--si round up, -B/--block-size units with and without a number (and their suffixes), the last of -b/-k/-m/-h/--si/-B winning, DU_BLOCK_SIZE/BLOCK_SIZE, and each directory or file counted once across operands. Apparent sizes still leave directories at 0, as coreutils 9.2+ does.
exclusions: The cross-filesystem effect of -x is deferred because it requires a separate disposable filesystem mount.
Other du options and error wording are not covered by this focused suite.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t identifies du as a builtin, as required for the loadable to be available with an empty executable PATH.
cases.script: type -t du

cases.purpose: The Bash help database exposes the documented short description embedded in the du loadable metadata.
cases.script: help -d du
cases.stdout: du - Estimate disk usage of files and directories.

cases.purpose: GNU du -b reports apparent byte sizes for multiple named regular files in argument order.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > alpha
printf '12345' > beta
du -b alpha beta

cases.purpose: With no path operand, GNU du uses the current directory; --bytes makes the one-file total independent of allocated blocks.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > leaf
du --bytes

cases.purpose: GNU du --all prints immediate files while --max-depth limits displayed entries; parent totals still include deeper files.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin mkdir -p tree/sub/leaf
printf 'x' > tree/top
printf 'yz' > tree/sub/middle
printf '123' > tree/sub/leaf/deep
du --all --bytes --max-depth=1 tree

cases.purpose: GNU du --null terminates each -a result with NUL, including a filename containing a space.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin mkdir tree
printf 'xy' > 'tree/space name'
printf 'z' > tree/plain
du --null --all --bytes tree

cases.purpose: Apparent byte counts rounded to 1024-byte units round each operand upward, while --total rounds the combined byte count.
cases.script:
printf '%1025s' '' > a
printf '%1023s' '' > b
du --apparent-size --block-size=1024 --total a b

cases.purpose: GNU du formats the same apparent 1500-byte file in binary human-readable units and decimal SI units.
cases.script:
printf '%1500s' '' > data
du --apparent-size --human-readable data
du --apparent-size --si data

cases.purpose: GNU du counts a hard-linked file once by default and twice with --count-links; the fixture also checks hard-link identity in the resulting tree.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin mkdir tree
printf 'abcde' > tree/original
PATH=/usr/bin ln tree/original tree/alias
du --bytes --summarize tree
du --bytes --count-links --summarize tree

cases.purpose: GNU du reports a symlink's own apparent size by default, follows a command-line link with -H, and follows nested links with -L while avoiding duplicate accounting of the target.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin mkdir tree
printf 'data' > tree/target
PATH=/usr/bin ln -s target tree/alias
du --bytes tree/alias
du --bytes -H tree/alias
du --bytes --summarize -L tree

cases.purpose: Check that -x excludes a nested directory on a different device while retaining the root filesystem total.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or controlled fixture with two mounted filesystems and a GNU du comparison across that boundary. The mandated runner does not provide a separate mounted fixture filesystem; do not attempt a mount in this suite.

cases.purpose: Deduplicate a regular file reached through multiple nested symbolic links under -L regardless of creation order; -l counts each link and -H preserves nested links. Repeated calls reset accounting.
cases.script:
mkdir tree
printf data > tree/target
ln -s target tree/alias
ln -s target tree/second
du -bLs tree
du -blLs tree
du -bHs tree
du -bLs tree

cases.purpose: Deduplicate a regular file reached through multiple nested symbolic links under -L regardless of creation order; -l counts each link and -H preserves nested links. Repeated calls reset accounting.
cases.script:
mkdir tree
ln -s target tree/alias
printf data > tree/target
ln -s target tree/second
du -bLs tree
du -blLs tree
du -bHs tree
du -bLs tree

cases.purpose: --exclude=PATTERN and -X/--exclude-from=FILE skip names whose path or a tail after '/' matches, including operands (guest pass 2, G33).
cases.script:
mkdir -p t/x/y t/z; : > t/f; : > t/x/a.o; : > t/x/y/b
echo '== x'; du --exclude=x t
echo '== t'; du --exclude=t t
echo '== *.o'; du -a --exclude='*.o' t | sort -k2
echo '== t/x'; du --exclude t/x t
echo '== x/y'; du --exclude='x/y' t
printf 'x\n*.o\n' > X
echo '== -X'; du -a -X X t | sort -k2
echo '== from'; du -a --exclude-from=X t | sort -k2

cases.purpose: --inodes counts inodes (hard links once unless -l) with -a, -s, -c and -h (guest pass 2, G33).
cases.script:
mkdir -p t/x/y t/z; : > t/f; : > t/x/a.o; : > t/x/y/b; ln t/f t/hl
du --inodes t | sort -k2
du --inodes -s t
du --inodes -s -l t
du --inodes -sh t
du --inodes -s -c t

cases.purpose: --files0-from=FILE (and - for stdin) takes NUL-separated operands; operands alongside it, an empty name and an unreadable list fail with status 1 (guest pass 2, G33).
cases.script:
mkdir -p t/x/y t/z
printf 't/x\0t/z\0' > L
du --files0-from=L
printf 't/z\0' | du --files0-from=-
du --files0-from=L t || echo rc=$?
printf 't/x\0\0' > L2
du --files0-from=L2 || echo rc=$?
du --files0-from=missing || echo rc=$?
du --exclude || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: GNU tools answer --help with help on stdout and status 0; du --help used to write usage to stderr or exit nonzero (guest pass 2, G38).
cases.script: du --help >o 2>e; echo rc=$?; [[ -s o && ! -s e ]] && echo stdout-only

cases.purpose: G90: GNU du's "cannot access 'NAME'" for missing operands, quoted, with the remaining operand still counted.
cases.script:
printf 'x\n' > f
{ du nosuch 'a b' f > /dev/null || echo rc=$?; } 2>err
sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //' err >&2
rm err

cases.purpose: du usage errors print GNU's message and "Try 'du --help' for more information." and exit 1 (they used to exit 2): unknown options, missing arguments, a bad --max-depth or block size, -a with -s, -s with --max-depth=N; -s -d 0 only warns (guest pass 7, G113).
cases.script:
s() { local rc=0; eval "$1" 2>&1 || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"; }
s 'du --bogus'
s 'du -Q'
s 'du -d x .'
s 'du --max-depth=x .'
s 'du -B x .'
s 'du --block-size=x .'
s 'du -as .'
s 'du -s -d 1 .'
s 'du -s -d 0 . >/dev/null'
s 'du -d'
s 'du --block-size'

cases.purpose: G144: GNU du -h and --si round up to one decimal below 10 and to a whole number from 10 on, moving to the next unit when a value rounds up to it (1048575 bytes is 1.0M); bash-os rounded to nearest. Sizes stay under the runner's 8 MiB file-size limit.
cases.script:
for s in 0 999 1000 1001 1023 1024 1025 9999 10239 10240 10241 102401 999999 1000001 1048575 1048577 5000000 8000000; do truncate -s $s z; printf '%s %s %s\n' $s "$(du -bh z | cut -f1)" "$(du --apparent-size --si z | cut -f1)"; done
mkdir many; for i in $(seq 1500); do : > many/$i; done
du --inodes -h many; du --inodes --si many

cases.purpose: G144: -B and --block-size take K, M, G, T, P, E (k, m, g, t), KB/MB (powers of 1000) and KiB forms; a unit without a number is printed after each amount (K, kB, MiB); C-notation numbers work; zero, a bad suffix and a size over 64 bits are GNU's three diagnostics with status 1. The script line prefix the shell adds to a builtin's message is removed.
cases.script:
s() { local rc=0 out; out=$(du -b "$@" z 2>&1) || rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; echo "rc=$rc"; }
truncate -s 8000000 z
for b in K M G T P E k m g KB kB MB mB KiB MiB 1K 1KB 1MiB 2KB 10K 0x10 010 +5 human-readable si 15E 0 0K 08 x '' 12x 1.5K p KK Pb 1Z ZB 16E 99999999999999999999; do printf '[%s] ' "$b"; s -B "$b"; done
for b in MB x Z 7x; do s --block-size="$b"; done

cases.purpose: G144: the last of -b, -k, -m, -h, --si, -B and --block-size decides the output unit (bash-os let -h and --si win wherever they were); BLOCK_SIZE and DU_BLOCK_SIZE set the default, the first one set deciding even when invalid.
cases.script:
truncate -s 8000000 z
for o in '-b -k -h' '-b -h -k' '-b -m -B 1' '-b -B 1 -m' '-h -b' '--si -b' '-b --si' '-b -BK -h' '-b -h -BK' '-b --si -BK' '-k --si --apparent-size' '-hk --apparent-size' '--block-size=human-readable -b' '--apparent-size -hm' '--apparent-size -mh'; do printf '%s: ' "$o"; du $o z; done
BLOCK_SIZE=K du --apparent-size z
DU_BLOCK_SIZE=M BLOCK_SIZE=K du --apparent-size z
DU_BLOCK_SIZE=x BLOCK_SIZE=K du --apparent-size z
BLOCKSIZE=KB du --apparent-size z
BLOCK_SIZE=si du --apparent-size z
BLOCK_SIZE=K du -b z

cases.purpose: G144: GNU du counts each directory and file once per run: a repeated operand, an operand inside an earlier one, or an earlier operand inside a later one is not counted again (and not printed), also for --inodes and -c totals; -l counts every name again. Directories add 0 to apparent sizes (coreutils 9.2+), so du -sb EMPTYDIR is 0.
cases.script:
mkdir -p t/a/b t/e emp
printf hello > t/f1
printf '%3000s' '' > t/a/f2
printf '%70000s' '' > t/a/b/f3
ln t/f1 t/a/hl
for o in '-sb emp' '-sb t t/a' '-sb t/a t' '-b t t' '-cb t/a t/a' '-acb t t/a' '-acb t/a t' '-cb t/a/f2 t/a/f2' '-ab t/a/f2 t/a' '-sb t/a/b t/a' '-cbl t/a t/a' '-s --inodes t t/a' '-s --inodes t/a t' '-csb t/a t' '-c --apparent-size -k t t/a'; do echo "== $o"; du $o | sort -k2; done
